results.title: integrating technology in early childhood classrooms
results.content: * How do early childhood preservice teachers use digital technology to teach and support young children’s learning? The frequency of use was observed to be high in the order of Instructional Use, Software-guided Use, Guided Use, and Free Use. Out of the 199 instances of TIS use in our data, approximately 60% (120 instances) were identified as Instructional Use, 33% (65 instances) as Software-guided Use, 5% (9 instances) as Guided Use, and 2% (5 instances) as Free Use. Our findings suggest that nearly 98% (194 instances) of technology use in early childhood classrooms is driven by explicit goals, mostly focusing on academic content learning including maths, literacy, science, and social studies. One of the findings indicates that early childhood preservice teachers primarily integrated technology into technology types of use where children have minimal to no agency in initiating and directing technological tools that are Instructional Use and Software-guided Use. The participants used technological devices and resources to meet explicit learning goals in academic content areas such as maths and literacy.

results.title: A systematic review of AI-powered chatbots for English as ...
results.content: # Transforming language education: A systematic review of AI-powered chatbots for English as a foreign language speaking practice. To analyze pertinent publications in the SSCI journals, a systematic review was conducted for this study, which investigates the trends of chatbots in education studies, with a focus on English speaking skills. Despite the increasing use of AI-powered chatbots in education, limited research has explored how to develop the merits of AI-powered chatbots in English-speaking teaching or learning. The empirical evidence of chatbot applications from 24 research studies conducted in an English-speaking learning environment and published between 2017 and 2023 was examined in this systematic review. The topic of study on chatbots in English language-speaking practice skills was determined to be in its early stages, which suggests that there is a lot of space for performing pertinent research to support creative English-speaking learning and work with chatbots to enhance learning results. Specifically, the study provides insights into the effectiveness of AI chatbots in enhancing students’ English-speaking learning outcomes, confidence, engagement and motivation.
